primitives.name: Snap Legality Check
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Intelligence value - **SCHEME** (primary): All-22 formation/alignment analysis — pre-snap legality, OL/WR alignment, officiating mechanics.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'L': 'legal formation indicator (dimensionless)', 'A_{ol}': 'offensive line alignment vector (meters)', 'A_{wr}': 'wide receiver alignment vector (meters)', 'T_{snap}': 'snap timing threshold (seconds)'}
primitives.assumptions: Pre-snap alignment must satisfy legal formation constraints within ±0.5 meters of official positioning.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Formation violation occurs when |A_{wr} - A_{ol}| > 0.5 m at t = T_{snap}

layer2.mapping: Each alignment vector maps to a probabilistic constraint in GSI's legal formation space; GSE uses this to compute snap-state transition probabilities.
layer2.telemetry: Frame-by-frame alignment deviation from official scrimmage line

primitives.name: Officiating Controversy Resolution
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **TRUST-SIGNAL** (secondary): officiating controversy resolution — settles "was it actually a penalty" debates with film evidence rather than narrative.
primitives.assumptions: Penalty is confirmed if F_{frame} = true and C_{judge} = false at snap moment.
primitives.breakdown_regime: P_{penalty} = 1 iff F_{frame} = true AND C_{judge} = false

layer2.mapping: Derives penalty likelihood from freeze-frame logic; GSE uses this to resolve contested calls in real time.
layer2.telemetry: Judge-side check flag and frame-level snap state

primitives.name: Receiver Alignment Verification
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **OL** (tertiary): line-of-scrimmage freeze frames occasionally show OL splits/alignments.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R_{align}': 'receiver alignment deviation (meters)', 'L_{scrimmage}': 'scrimmage line position (meters)', 'T_{check}': 'alignment check timestamp (seconds)'}
primitives.assumptions: Alignment deviation exceeds 0.3 meters from scrimmage line triggers verification.
primitives.breakdown_regime: R_{align} > 0.3 m at T_{check} implies potential offside

layer2.mapping: Receiver alignment vector maps to GSI's offside detection kernel; GSE uses this to validate receiver positioning during snap.
